THE PORTRAIT EDIT
ISSUE 02 / OCTOBER 2026
GLOSSARY
003
A language for looking
GLOSSARY / 1 OF 2
High-key
A predominantly light image with bright backgrounds and
restrained shadows. It describes the overall tonal
treatment, rather than simply an overexposed photograph.
Shallow depth of field
A narrow zone of sharp focus that leaves foreground or
background details soft, helping separate the subject from
the scene.
Rim light
Light from behind or beside a subject that traces a bright
edge around hair, clothing or the silhouette.
Film grain
The visible texture associated with photographic film. In a
digital prompt it usually requests a similar textured
appearance.
Kodak Portra
A family of color-negative photographic films often used for
portraits. In a prompt, the name suggests a film-inspired
color and tonal treatment.
Seamless backdrop
A continuous studio background without a visible join
between the wall and floor, keeping attention on the
subject.
Muted palette
A color scheme with restrained saturation. Colors appear
subdued rather than vivid or electric.
Soft focus
A deliberately gentle rendering of detail and edges. It can
suggest a dreamy image, beyond simply blurring the
background.
Diffused light
Light spread through a broad source or scattering material
to soften the transition between light and shadow.
Close-up
A tight framing that concentrates on a face or a small group
of details, excluding much of the surrounding scene.
Full-length
A framing that includes the entire person from head to toe,
often used to show a complete outfit.
Mid-stride
A pose captured during a step, suggesting walking motion
rather than a static stance.
